venue: Punch Bowl Social at The Battery, Atlanta
blurb:
The Wednesday before Thanksgiving has exactly one job: get the holiday weekend started right. Punch Bowl Social at The Battery is ready to help.

Drinksgiving runs from 7 to 10pm with all-day happy hour (yes, all day), a live DJ from 7 to 10, board games everywhere, and food and drink specials starting at $5. It's the unofficial pre-holiday, and they're treating it like an actual holiday. Bring your competitive side, bring someone fun, and leave the Thursday prep for Thursday morning.

No cover, no reservations required. Just show up and enjoy the fact that most people have the next four days off.
scoring_notes: Drinksgiving is a recognized pre-Thanksgiving tradition that plays well with the young professional segment of the Perimeter audience. Adult-skewing event with low barrier to entry. The Battery location is familiar and accessible. Slightly lower uniqueness since this is a recurring annual format, but the specific date hook (night before Thanksgiving) gives it seasonal relevance. $5 specials are a fun detail for any income level.

event_name: Guided Tasting & Tour at ASW Distillery
venue: ASW Distillery at The Battery, Atlanta
blurb:
Sunday afternoon, good whiskey, and a peek behind the curtain at how it's actually made. That's the whole pitch, and it's a pretty good one.

ASW Distillery's Guided Tasting and Tour takes you through four pours of their award-winning spirits, then brings you back into the distillery itself for a look at the copper hybrid still where their gin and vodka come to life. It's approachable if you're new to craft spirits and interesting enough if you're not. The Battery location means you can grab dinner or catch something else after without having to move your car.

Sunday at 2pm is an easy yes. Grab a spot before it fills up.
scoring_notes: Solid event for the adult-leaning Perimeter audience. Good Sunday afternoon option with low barrier to entry. Slightly lower uniqueness since distillery tours are more common as a category, but the specific ASW experience and Battery location add appeal. $105K HHI makes pricing a non-factor. Good fallback if the Friday Infusions class is already full.

event_name: Roswell Dance Theatre presents The Nutcracker
venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb:
The Nutcracker is one of those things that sounds like a tradition but actually has to earn its place every year. Roswell Dance Theatre earns it.

This production runs at the Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center from November 27 through December 6, with ten shows across the run including four meet-and-greet performances where the kids can get photos and autographs with the characters after the show. The cast mixes world-class professional dancers with students from the Tolbert Yilmaz School of Dance, and the production itself, directed by Nancy Tolbert Yilmaz and her team, has a real reputation in this area. This is not a school recital with a Tchaikovsky backing track.

For families with kids who've never seen a live ballet, this is the one to start with. For empty nesters who've been before, the Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center is a genuinely beautiful place to spend a holiday evening. Tickets are on sale now at RoswellNutcracker.com.
scoring_notes: Sandy Springs is squarely in the Perimeter coverage area. The mixed audience of young families and empty nesters is an ideal fit for a Nutcracker production. The professional-student hybrid cast and 10-show run give it more weight than a typical community ballet. Meet-and-greet shows add family appeal. The holiday timing works strongly in its favor as a seasonal anchor event.

event_name: Thanksgiving Cocktail Class at ASW Distillery
venue: ASW Distillery at The Battery, Atlanta
blurb:
Thanksgiving is three days out. This is how you get ahead of it.

ASW Distillery's Thanksgiving Cocktail Class gives each guest their own fully stocked bar station and walks you through building three cocktails from scratch, using their award-winning whiskey, vodka, and gin. By the end you'll know the fundamentals of balance, technique, and what to actually do when someone asks you to "make something" at the holiday table. The skills carry forward well beyond Thursday.

It runs from 2 to 5pm on Sunday the 22nd at The Battery. If you've been meaning to actually learn this stuff instead of just winging it, this is a good window. Spots won't last long this close to the holiday.
scoring_notes: The Thanksgiving timing gives this class a timely, seasonal hook that elevates it above a standard cocktail class. Strong fit for young professionals and couples. The $105K HHI makes pricing comfortable. Adult-skewing which matches the Perimeter newsletter audience. The practical 'learn a skill before the holiday' angle is a strong selling point for this demographic.

venue: ASW Distillery at The Battery, Atlanta
blurb:
This is a Friday night that actually teaches you something useful.

ASW Distillery's Infusions 101 class walks you through the art of spirit infusions: fruits, herbs, spices, botanicals, all blended into their award-winning Bustletown Vodka. You'll taste three finished liqueurs, pick the one you want to make, and go home with a liter of vodka and a recipe card to finish it yourself over the next few days. It's interactive, it's low-key, and it's genuinely the kind of skill that makes you a more interesting person at holiday parties.

The Battery is easy to get to and parking is a non-issue. Two hours, good drinks, and you walk out with something to show for it. That's a solid Friday.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for young professionals and couples in the Perimeter audience. $105K HHI makes a craft cocktail class a comfortable spend. Friday evening timing is ideal. The 'take something home' angle adds value beyond just a night out. Adult-skewing which matches the newsletter's lean. Slightly lower uniqueness since ASW runs multiple class formats, but Infusions 101 is a distinct and specific offering.

blurb:
You've probably never stood in front of a propane forge, hammer in hand, shaping a piece of iron into something you'll actually use. That's exactly what makes this worth doing.

Bladesmithing 101 at Art Center West in Roswell is a two-day, hands-on workshop where you'll walk through the whole process: tools, materials, forging technique, heat treating, and finishing. You leave with a 3-piece knife set you made yourself. Not a kit. Not a paint-and-sip situation. An actual thing you built from raw metal with your own hands.

This is a genuinely rare experience, the kind you'd normally have to drive to the middle of nowhere to find. It's right in Roswell. Spots are limited by nature, so if this sounds like your kind of weekend, don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness score because bladesmithing workshops are genuinely rare and experiential. Appeals to the young professional and DIY-curious segment of the audience. The $105K HHI makes workshop pricing comfortable. Skews slightly more male and adventure-oriented but the broader 'unique experience' angle plays well for the Perimeter mix. November 14 falls on a Saturday, within the eligible window.

blurb:
If you've ever cranked "Seven Nation Army" so loud the neighbors probably heard it, this one is not a drill.

Jack White is coming to Coca-Cola Roxy on Friday, November 20, and this is exactly the kind of show that gets talked about for years after. He's one of the most unpredictable live performers working right now. The setlists change, the energy is unhinged in the best possible way, and no two shows feel the same. You're not watching someone run through a greatest hits playlist on autopilot. You're watching a guy who genuinely seems like he might combust on stage.

Coca-Cola Roxy is one of the best mid-size venues in Atlanta, which means you're close enough to actually feel it. This is a weeknight show worth the late bedtime. Grab your tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 is squarely in the wheelhouse of Jack White's core fanbase, who grew up with The White Stripes in their teens and twenties. Adult-skewing audience with disposable income at $105K HHI makes concert ticket pricing a non-issue. Coca-Cola Roxy is a well-known, comfortable venue for this demographic. High uniqueness since this is a specific ticketed show, not recurring.

event_name: Friday the 13th with the KSU Wind Ensemble
blurb:
It's Friday the 13th, it's a university wind ensemble, and the program is called Roaring Thunder featuring an electric guitar soloist. That combination is either your thing or it isn't, and if it's your thing, this Friday night is a GIFT.

The KSU Wind Ensemble has spent nearly three decades pushing what a contemporary wind ensemble can actually do, and tonight's program leans into that fully. D.J. Sparr's Zepher Roaring Thunder gets the spotlight, with Sean Thrower on electric guitar alongside the ensemble. It's not your grandfather's concert band. The Friday the 13th timing is a fun coincidence, Morgan Concert Hall is a great room, and it's right up the road.

If you've never caught a KSU ensemble performance, this is a solid introduction to what they do over there.
scoring_notes: Lower demographic fit because university ensemble concerts appeal to a narrower slice of the East Cobb audience, primarily those with a classical or band music background. The electric guitar soloist and Friday the 13th programming add novelty that lifts it above a standard academic recital. Included as the eighth event because it's a real, specific, upcoming event with a distinctive program, but it's the weakest fit of the eight.

event_name: Murder Mystery Dinner Theater at Hudson Grille Kennesaw
blurb:
Date night, friend group outing, or something to do with the in-laws over the holiday weekend before everyone descends for Thanksgiving. The Murder Mystery Co. dinner show at Hudson Grille in Kennesaw checks all three boxes.

You get a three-course meal, a fully interactive whodunit where you're either playing detective or playing suspect, and two to three hours of something way more memorable than another dinner where everyone stares at their phones. The mysteries rotate every month so it's not the same show if you've been before.

It's local, it's low-commitment, and it's the kind of night where someone in your group ends up being the killer and that becomes a story you tell for years. Friday the 20th, 6:30pm. Worth grabbing a spot.
scoring_notes: Strong audience match for couples and social groups in this demographic, especially with Thanksgiving week approaching and out-of-town guests in the picture. Local Kennesaw venue is a plus. Slight deduction on uniqueness because Murder Mystery Co. is a franchise format that runs monthly, making it less of a true can't-miss. But the holiday timing and interactive social nature lift it for this audience.

event_name: The Nutcracker presented by Roswell Dance Theatre
venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb:
The holiday season officially starts when you're sitting in a darkened theater watching Clara head off to the Kingdom of Sweets. And Roswell Dance Theatre has been doing this production long enough that it's become the real thing for a lot of North Atlanta families.

The run kicks off November 27th at the Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center with ten performances spread across two weekends. World-class professional dancers sharing the stage with RDT students and younger performers from the Tolbert Yilmaz School makes this feel like a community event and a legitimate production at the same time. There are meet-and-greet shows if you've got younger kids or grandkids coming in for the holiday.

If this is already a tradition in your house, you know what to do. If you've never been, this is a good year to start.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's mix of established families with teen or college-age kids and empty nesters means Nutcracker has solid but not universal appeal. Grandparents visiting for Thanksgiving is a real use case here. Sandy Springs venue is nearby. Slight audience match deduction because the demographic skews older and may not have young children at home anymore, but the holiday tradition angle and multi-generational appeal still play well.

blurb:
Free admission, rare cars, and a Saturday morning with nowhere to be. That's the whole pitch, and honestly it doesn't need much more than that.

The 7th Annual Roswell Motoring Festival is back at Roswell City Hall this Saturday after getting pushed from its original October date. We're talking collectors bringing out vehicles from every era, some of which you genuinely don't see on the road or at typical car shows. Boats and motorcycles in the mix too. There's a coffee barista on site, food vendors, and a photo booth if you want to make something of it.

It benefits the Roswell First Responders Foundation, which is a solid reason to show up beyond the cars themselves. Bring the family or bring a buddy who'd appreciate spending an hour walking through automotive history. It costs you nothing.
scoring_notes: East Cobb homeowners at $118K median income skew heavily toward car enthusiasm and outdoor weekend activities. Free admission removes any friction. The rescheduled date gives it a slightly unusual context. Family-friendly without being kid-focused, which fits the mix of established families and empty nesters well. Slight uniqueness deduction because car shows, while not monthly, aren't rare events in metro Atlanta.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
If Love Actually is already in your Thanksgiving weekend rotation, this year you can watch it the way it was always meant to be experienced: with a full live orchestra performing Craig Armstrong's score while the film plays on screen.

The entire cast is there in the film. Hugh Grant, Emma Thompson, Liam Neeson, Colin Firth, Bill Nighy, all of them. But the music, which does more emotional heavy lifting in that movie than most people realize, is live. Right in front of you. At Cobb Energy, which is a beautiful room for it.

It's Black Friday. The mall will still be there. This is a better use of the evening, and it's the kind of thing you'll actually remember from the holiday.
scoring_notes: Love Actually sits squarely in the cultural sweet spot for 38-50 year old East Cobb residents, particularly women but with strong cross-gender appeal. Black Friday evening timing is genuinely smart positioning. Live orchestra format is a meaningful upgrade from watching it at home. Strong uniqueness because this specific touring concert production doesn't come through Atlanta every year.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
Picture your favorite rock and metal songs, the ones that defined your high school and college years, rebuilt from the ground up with a full orchestra, in a candlelit concert hall. That's exactly what The Rock Orchestra by Candlelight is, and it's coming to Cobb Energy on November 21st.

This isn't a novelty act. They've done over 400 shows and drawn half a million people in four years. The concept works because they're not watering anything down. The power is still there. The darkness is still there. It just hits differently when you're hearing it surrounded by strings and candlelight.

If you've been to a Candlelight concert series show before, you know the vibe. If you haven't, this is a great first one. It's a genuinely different kind of Friday night out.
scoring_notes: The Candlelight concert format has strong traction with 35-50 age groups who want a grown-up night out that isn't just dinner. Rock and metal repertoire fits East Cobb's median age well. Cobb Energy venue is conveniently close. Slight deduction on uniqueness because Candlelight-format shows have proliferated in Atlanta, but this specific production is distinctive enough to stand out.

event_name: Sweet Baby James: The #1 James Taylor Tribute
blurb:
If James Taylor was the soundtrack to your college years, your first apartment, or basically any road trip you took in the 80s and 90s, this one is worth clearing your Saturday night for.

Bill Griese brought this show to Roswell last year and it sold out. So they brought him back. No impersonations, no corniness, just someone who genuinely knows how to play the music the way it was meant to sound. Fire and Rain, You've Got a Friend, Shower the People, all of it. And it's right here in your backyard at the Roswell Cultural Arts Center, which is a genuinely great room for this kind of show.

It sold out last time. That's not filler, that's a data point. Get your tickets before you're watching it sell out again from the sidelines.
scoring_notes: James Taylor is essentially custom-made for a 42 median age, established-household East Cobb audience. Local venue, sold-out history, and a Saturday night slot make this a natural fit. Slightly lower uniqueness score because it's a tribute act and not the real thing, but the sold-out precedent and neighborhood convenience are strong selling points.

blurb:
Jack White doesn't do residencies. He doesn't play the same city six nights in a row. When he shows up, he shows up once, and then he's gone. Saturday, November 21st at Coca-Cola Roxy is that night for Atlanta.

If you grew up on the White Stripes and watched him build one of the most restless, genre-defying solo careers in rock, you already know what this show is going to feel like. Raw. Loud. Genuinely unpredictable. The Battery is a perfect setup for it too, so you can grab dinner, walk over, and make a real night out of it.

Tickets are moving. This is not a "I'll check back next week" situation. Grab them now and lock it in.
scoring_notes: East Cobb skews 42 median age, which is squarely in the White Stripes/early Jack White era fanbase. High income means ticket price is not a barrier. One-night show at a great venue with no recurring equivalent makes this a true can't-miss. The Battery location adds a full evening out, which appeals to both couples and friend groups in this demographic.

event_name: Holiday Cookie Crawl on Marietta Square
time: Evening (check Marietta Square for exact hours)
blurb:
The holidays are officially starting on Marietta Square this Friday, and this is the event that kicks it all off.

The Holiday Cookie Crawl, presented by the Georgia Symphony Orchestra, runs alongside Candlelight Shopping, the traditional start to the holiday season on the Square. You get a collectible bag and a passport, then work your way through 12 local businesses collecting 12 different cookies from local bakeries along the way. It's part scavenger hunt, part holiday stroll, part excuse to drag the whole family out of the house before the season really gets going.

The Square is going to be lit up, the shops are open, and there's plenty of room to grab dinner or drinks in between stops. This is the kind of evening that actually feels like the holidays, not just another errand run. If you've been waiting for the season to start, this is your sign.
scoring_notes: Marietta Square is East Cobb's backyard. This is a family-friendly event that also works for couples and empty nesters. It's the official holiday kickoff for the area, which makes it genuinely can't-miss for the week. High demographic fit across the board.
